title: From Australian Minimum Wage to Annual Salary: Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with the Australian way. Understand the 38-hour week, casual loading of 25%, and super paid on top. Use our timesheet for your base rate.
salarySummary: Based on the Australian minimum wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is about $52,254 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary in Australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time job, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. If you are casual, add 25% loading to your base rate first, then use the same formula. This gives a gross annual figure before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave) and other entitlements. For the Australian minimum wage, the base rate is $26.44 per hour, so with casual loading it becomes $33.05 per hour. When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate in the formula: $33.05 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $65,318 per year (gross). Super is then calculated on that loaded amount.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my annual pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your salary; your employer adds it separately. For example, if your annual gross pay is $60,000, your super contribution would be $7,200 (12% of $60,000), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The super amount is not included in your take-home pay or taxable income.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay

When you are offered an hourly rate or a salary, knowing the annual equivalent helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, and most calculations use that figure. The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours every week, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

This article focuses on the [australian minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and how casual loading and superannuation affect your total compensation. We use figures from the Fair Work Commission, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office to give you a reliable estimate.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026, the minimum wage is **$26.44 per hour**, which equals **$1,004.90 per week** for a 38-hour week. This is the legal floor; many workers receive more under their award or enterprise agreement.

Award rates are industry-specific minimums that often include penalty rates, allowances, and different classifications. They are higher than the National Minimum Wage for most roles. If you are covered by an award, your minimum hourly rate will be specified in that award. The [pay guides](/blog) on our site can help you find the right rate for your job.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on their base hourly rate to compensate for not having paid leave (annual leave, personal leave) and other benefits. This loading is added to the minimum wage or award rate. For the Australian minimum wage, the casual rate is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25).

When you use our [timesheet](/), you enter your **base hourly rate** (the rate before casual loading). If you are casual, check the box to add 25% loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. The calculator will then show your annual gross pay including the loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution your employer makes to your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is **12% of your ordinary earnings**. Ordinary earnings include your base rate, casual loading, and most allowances, but not overtime. The super is paid **on top** of your salary, not deducted from it.

For example, if your annual gross pay (including casual loading) is $65,318, your employer must contribute $7,838 (12% of $65,318) to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super does not appear in your take-home pay or your taxable income. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) on our site.

### Fortnightly Pay and Weekly Pay

Many Australian workers are paid fortnightly (every two weeks). To find your fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the minimum wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80 before tax. If you are casual, weekly pay is $1,255.90 ($33.05 × 38) and fortnightly is $2,511.80.

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing to salary offers that are quoted per year or per month.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. There are reductions for low-income earners, but the thresholds for 2026–27 were not confirmed in this estimate; we use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for estimates.

For a full-time worker on the minimum wage ($52,254 gross), the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $7,600, leaving a take-home pay of about $44,654 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed estimate.

### Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for full-time adult ordinary time. As of May 2026, that figure is **$2,083.70 per week**. This is an average across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job. Your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your occupation, experience, and location. See our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more context.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Using Our Reference Tables

For a quick comparison of different hourly rates and their annual equivalents, visit our [reference tables](/data). They show gross annual pay, estimated tax, and super for a range of hourly rates, assuming a 38-hour week.

### Summary

- **Formula**: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours for full-time).
- **Australian minimum wage**: $26.44 per hour, $1,004.90 per week, $52,254 per year.
- **Casual loading**: add 25% to base rate. Minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.
- **Super**: 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings, up to $270,830.
- **Tax**: progressive scale plus 2% Medicare levy.

Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see your own figures. Remember that award rates, enterprise agreements, and individual contracts may set higher minimums. Always check your specific award or agreement for your correct rate.
